candidates.tagline: Hyundai's Atlas kicked a ball at the World Cup; its factory workers kicked back with the first humanoid robot strike ever
candidates.story: Hyundai deployed Boston Dynamics' Atlas robots to deliver the match ball at the FIFA World Cup on July 5 as a PR stunt, then 39,000 Hyundai factory workers launched the first-ever humanoid robot factory strike on July 13, demanding a say before Atlas enters their plants.
candidates.why_funny: The same company that paid millions to showcase its human-replacement robots at the world's biggest sporting event triggered the first worker rebellion against those exact robots within two weeks.
candidates.alt: Boston Dynamics' Atlas humanoid robot standing in an industrial promotional setting with Hyundai branding, the white and black bipedal robot looking both impressive and faintly ominous next to a Hyundai vehicle

candidates.tagline: A sandwich chain mentioned AI 22 times in its IPO filing. It sells sandwiches.
candidates.story: Jersey Mike's Subs filed its IPO documents in July 2026 mentioning 'artificial intelligence' or 'AI' 22 times — more than weather (5 times) or lightning (0 times), despite a location being struck by lightning in 2021 — because 'AI' is apparently what unlocks investor dollars when you sell cold cuts.
candidates.why_funny: They dropped AI four times more often than they mentioned weather in an IPO for a business whose core technology is a deli slicer, and the investment banks apparently nodded along.
candidates.alt: An AI-generated illustration of a glowing surreal sandwich with neural network patterns woven into the bread and fillings, representing the absurd collision of AI hype and the sandwich industry
